newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Glaverbel 96 group net, current profit up.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Glaverbel 96 group net, current profit up.

text.p: Full year 1996 earnings
(billion Belgian francs unless stated)
Group net (excludes minorities) 1.768 vs 0.621
Consolidated net profit 1.915 vs 0.796
Current gross profit 1.442 vs 1.224
Operating profit 2.732 vs 2.987
Gross operating cashflow 6.584 vs 6.959
Consolidated sales 38.663 vs 38.246
NOTE - Belgian glass maker Glaverbel is controlled by Japan's Asahi Glass Co. Ltd.. Glaverbel made an extraordinary profit of 606 million francs.

This included a previously announced net capital gain of 1.166 billion francs from the sale last August of Glaverbel's stake in U.S. glass group AFG Industries, which was partly offset by the provision for payroll liabilities associated with cost cutting programmes already negotiated.
AFG's contribution to earnings amounted to 101 million francs in 1996 compared with 453 million the year before.
Consolidated sales rose 1.0 percent from 1995 on the changed consolidation perimeter, or 1.6 percent on a comparable basis.
This was despite heavy pressure on prices, which in European markets fell between 10 and 20 percent for raw glass. The recovery of some weaker currencies partly offset the price fall.
Volumes and prices of raw glass touched historic lows in the first half of 1996. The second half saw quantities recovering significantly but no improvement in prices, the company said.
Consolidated operating profit dropped 8.5 percent, or 6.7 percent on a comparable consolidation basis, but with the fall limited by cost control and an ongoing productivity drive.
Glaverbel said the 18 percent rise in current gross profit was due to a significant reduction in financial expenditure.
Net financial expenditure fell to 1.332 billion francs from 2.158 billion in 1995, as a result of financial restructuring, shedding the AFG stake and more favourable interest rates.

The group's debt to equity ratio stood at 0.72 at the end of 1996 (0.63 after deducting debt represented by the group's treasury shares) after the various acquisitions and divestments during the year, down from 0.97 at the end of 1995.

Glaverbel chief executive officer Luc Willame told a news conference a normal debt to equity ratio target for the industry was 0.5, though this was not a specific target for Glaverbel, whose ratio would vary "depending on what projects we had".
Willame said net debt at the end of 1996 was 14.5 billion francs, down from 21 billion at the end of 1995.

The change in the consolidation perimeter included 50 percent proportional consolidation for the Schott-Glaverbel joint venture, the disappearance of the Sovitec beads activity sold in December 1995 and the first time consolidation of processing companies newly acquired during the financial year.
The departure of AFG and the arrival of AST, which produces car windscreens, did not impact consolidated sales figures, Glaverbel said.
